title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration in Freshdesk
snippet:
The Freshworks Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI tools like Cursor and Claude to securely connect and interact with Freshdesk. The MCP server acts as middleware to expose specific capabilities, such as creating tickets, by using public APIs and supported authentication methods.

Note: Currently, Freshdesk allows you to authenticate requests involved in MCP integration by using an API key only.

```
This feature applies to the following products:
• Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (Latest version)
• Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026
```
Starting September 10, 2026, the Freshworks MCP integration is generally available. The rate limits and monthly action allowances for each plan are outlined below.
```
What counts as an MCP action?
An action is defined as a successful tool invocation via MCP. Examples of tool invocations. Examples:
• Fetch conversation related to the ticket with ID 1001 (1 action)
• Update the company name for the record with ID 11 to Apple (1 action)
```
| Supported plans | Rate limits (actions per minute) | Included MCP actions (per account, annually) |
|---|---|---|
| Growth | 25 | 1,200 |
| Pro | 50 | 6,000 |
| Enterprise | 100 | 12,000 |
```
Important:
• Pricing: To view current pricing and purchase add-on action packs, see Pricing.
• EAP transition:
• If you were on the Early Access Program (EAP), standard pricing and limits take effect on October 5, 2026.
• During the EAP, if you used the MCP integration on any plan other than Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (the latest version) or Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026 variant, the integration will stop working after September 10, 2026.
```
## **Supported MCP integrations**
Freshdesk supports MCP integration with any AI tool that provides MCP support. This section highlights a selection of commonly used integrations that you can connect to Freshdesk.
- Claude Code
- Claude Desktop
- [Cursor](http://Set-up-MCP-integration-with-Cursor)
- Microsoft Copilot Studio
- Visual Studio Code

To connect Claude Desktop to your MCP server, follow these steps:
1. Open Claude Desktop and go to Claude > Settings > Developer.

title: MCP Integration: Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
snippet:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables AI assistants, such as Claude and Microsoft Copilot, to connect directly to Freshdesk. Through MCP, these assistants can perform actions on your behalf, such as creating tickets, updating contacts, or retrieving conversation history, without leaving the AI client.
Which Freshdesk products support MCP?
MCP is supported only in Freshdesk 2021 and Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026. Following is the compatibility matrix:
| **Product / Plan Variant** | **GA Support (Post-Sep 10, 2026)** | **Notes** |
|---|---|---|
| Freshdesk Standalone 2021 (Latest version) | Supported | Full support for GA release. |
| Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026 | Supported | Full support for GA release. |
| Legacy Freshdesk Variants (Pre-2021) / Other SKUs | Not Supported | EAP access ends September 10, 2026. |
Which AI clients are supported?
You can use any AI client that supports the MCP standard. Connect your preferred MCP-compatible client to Freshdesk using the MCP server URL and the API key provided in your Freshdesk administrator settings.
### Setup and configuration
How do I find my MCP settings in Freshdesk?
Go to Admin Settings > Apps & Integrations > MCP. On the MCP Details page, you can copy your MCP server URL, generate an API key, and manage your connection.

How does authentication work for MCP?
Freshdesk MCP uses API key authentication. Each user manually connects their AI client using their individual Freshdesk API key and the MCP server URL. You can find your API key in your Freshdesk profile settings.

Not yet. Freshdesk is not currently listed as a native connector in AI client marketplaces. To connect an AI client to Freshdesk via MCP, you must manually enter the MCP server URL and authenticate using your API key.

title: Introduction
snippet:
**Freshdesk MCP** is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server that connects a [Freshdesk](https://www.freshdesk.com/) account to any MCP-compatible AI model or client. It exposes the Freshdesk API as a set of **tools** and **prompts** that can be invoked in natural language: the assistant can thus read and manage tickets, conversations, contacts, companies, knowledge base and custom fields.
The server is written in Python (FastMCP) with modular architecture (`core` / `services` / `schemas` / `tools`) and a shared HTTP client with rate limit management.
## What is it for¶
Once the server is connected, you can ask the assistant things like:
- "Show me ticket #12345 and its entire conversation"
- "Search for open and urgent tickets and assign them to the Support group"
- "Find the Acme company and create a contact for [mario.rossi@acme.it](mailto:mario.rossi@acme.it)"
- "Add a private note to ticket #12345 with analysis results"
- "Create a knowledge base article about resetting your password"
The model automatically chooses the correct tool and composes its parameters.
## Feature overview¶
- **124 tools exposed by MCP server**: 64 canonical `freshdesk_*` names and 60 legacy aliases deprecated. The aliases are associated with 59 handlers; `freshdesk_search_companies` exposes two of them.
- **2 guided prompts** (`create_ticket`, `create_reply`) to assist the model in composing payloads.
- **ToolAnnotations** on each tool (read / write / update / delete): behavior hints for safer automations.
- **Multi-tenant via HTTP**: a single deployment can serve multiple Freshdesk accounts, with credentials provided per-request.
- **Authentication via header** (`X-Freshdesk-Domain` / `X-Freshdesk-Api-Key`) preferred to query string.
- **Read-only** mode on tickets via `FRESHDESK_TICKETS_READ_ONLY`.
- **Context-safe attachments**: metadata is returned by default, base64 content only on request (1 MiB per file and 5 MiB overall by default).
- **Automatic pagination** of the conversation thread, up to 50 pages of 100 messages.
